_comment: Two sub-users, and the server gets no delete permission at all.
Pruning is done by BUCKET LIFECYCLE RULES, configured once in the Wasabi
console — never by the box. That is the whole point: ransomware, or a bug,
or a careless command on this server cannot erase the backup history,
because the credential it holds is physically unable to delete an object.
Neither user gets BypassGovernanceRetention: GOVERNANCE mode protects the
objects from everything except a deliberate act by the account root, which
is the escape hatch that COMPLIANCE mode would not leave us.
Lifecycle rules to configure on auditisa-dr (console):
db/daily/    expire after 90 days   (~540 restore points at 6 runs/day)
all prefixes NoncurrentVersionExpiration 90 days  (Object Lock forces
versioning on, and _LATEST.json is rewritten 6x a day)
Nothing is shorter than 90 days: Wasabi bills a 90-day minimum per object,
so a 14- or 30-day expiry costs exactly the same and only loses recoverability.
auditisa-archive holds the WORM copies and expires nothing.
